title: Tools to Streamline in situ Structural Analysis Using Cryo-ET
content: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is an emerging technique that enables the visualization of cellular landscapes in three dimensions at nanometer-scale resolution. When combined with sub-volume averaging (SVA), this technique can be used to visualize macromolecules within their native environment at near-atomic resolution. Two prevalent challenges in cryo-ET and SVA are: 1) the accurate identification and localization of proteins from cellular environments, and 2) the complexity of workflows for cryo-ET/SVA image analysis. First, to overcome issues with molecular crowding, missing-wedge distortions, and the increasing size of tomographic datasets, we developed MiLoPYP, a two-step, contrastive learning-based framework that allows for rapid molecular pattern discovery followed by precise protein localization. MiLoPYP can detect and localize a wide range of targets, enabling high-resolution SVA analysis of globular, tubular, and membrane-attached complexes. Second, to facilitate the execution of complex image analysis pipelines on datasets with thousands of tilt-series while leveraging recent machine learning-based advances in tomogram denoising, segmentation, particle picking, and 3D heterogeneity analysis, we have incorporated many of these tools into our scalable and easy-to-use web-based application, nextPYP. Together, these packages will contribute to improve the usability of tools for cryo-ET/SVA image analysis and streamline workflows for in situ structure determination.
